sourceFile: Diocesan resource page, fetched directly from https://www.dioceseli.org/cycle-prayer (a 12-month accordion widget, one <ol> of daily entries per month, Jan 1 - Dec 31 including a Feb 29 entry -- 366 entries total, no year stated anywhere on the page, evidently meant to repeat annually including in leap years).
notes: This source fits neither this schema's 'dated' nor 'monthly-recurring' cycleType -- it is a full annual cycle (366 distinct daily entries, different content on every single day) with no calendar year stated anywhere, explicitly including a Feb 29 entry ('The Black Clergy Caucus') for leap years. Per Josh's direct decision 2026-09-29 (the same kind of call that added 'monthly-recurring' for Arkansas), a new cycleType 'annual-recurring' (month+day, no year) was added to the schema for this shape rather than forcing it into either existing one.

The overwhelming majority of entries (250 of 366) follow one consistent 'Congregation Name, Place' comma format (place sometimes itself two-part, e.g. 'St. Paul's, Carroll Street, Brooklyn' -- Congregation, Neighborhood, Borough); these are transcribed as `parish` subjects, split on the FIRST comma (name = before, place = everything after, preserving a two-part place as printed).

One entry (December 25: 'Diocesan Convention: The Bishop, Convention Officers, Clerical and Lay Delegates') uses a colon-introduced descriptive list rather than the usual name/place comma pattern -- recorded as a single `category` subject with the full text preserved, not split on its internal commas.

Two entries (August 15 and August 29, both 'St. Mary's Shelter Island') are missing the source's own usual comma before the place, evidently a formatting slip -- transcribed as `parish` ('St. Mary's', place 'Shelter Island') since Shelter Island is a specific, unambiguous Long Island place name with no other plausible reading, not a guess.

Three entries appear to be congregation names but carry no place at all, in a source that otherwise always appends one for a real congregation (September 14 'Iglesia de la Santa Cruz'; October 5 and December 11, two slightly different renderings of 'Iglesia de San Francisco'/'Iglesia San Francisco') -- rather than inventing a place, these are recorded as `category` subjects with the name preserved exactly as printed (including the October/December spelling difference, itself preserved as a possible source inconsistency, not corrected).

Cross-referenced dioceses of the same TEC ecclesiastical province ('Province II - The Diocese of X') are recorded as `category` subjects, not `parish` (they are not Long Island's own congregations) -- the source's own inconsistent spacing/hyphenation across occurrences ('Province II - The Diocese of Western New York' vs 'Province II-Diocese of Western New York' vs 'Province II -  The Diocese of Haiti' with a double space) is preserved exactly as printed in each individual entry, not normalized to one style.

Two entries name a school/hospital bearing a saint's name rather than a congregation (April 7 "St. Mark's Day School"; October 25 "St. John's Episcopal Hospital") -- recorded as `category`, consistent with this corpus's existing precedent (Delaware's St. Anne's School, Chicago's campus ministries) that an institution is not a `parish` merely because its own name includes a saint's name or 'Church'/'Chapel'.
Apostrophes preserved exactly as printed in the source (a straight ' throughout, e.g. "St. John's").
